description: A team of CSE students participating in our first hackathon. Driven by logic, learning something new every day, and fueled by coffee :D
summary:
Mission Lunara is an interactive, story-driven educational game developed by team NovaSolaris, where players step into the role of a lunar researcher stationed at Shackleton Crater on the Moon’s south pole.

Over four challenges, players must manage a lunar research base, protect its resources, and make important decisions to keep the mission running. 
From dealing with power shortages to protecting greenhouse crops and transmitting research back to Earth, every decision comes with its own consequences. It combines learning, problem-solving, and creativity to encourage curiosity about space exploration.
Our goal is to make astronomy more engaging for younger audiences. Instead of simply reading about lunar exploration, players get to experience the challenges astronauts might face through interactive scenarios inspired by real scientific concepts and NASA data.
details:
When developing Mission Lunara, our team wanted to create something that replaces the traditional educational game. We wanted players to feel involved in the learning process rather than simply reading information or answering questions.

We built the game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML is used to structure the interface of the game, CSS helped create the pixel art visuals and the space-themed atmosphere, and JavaScript allowed us to bring the game come to life through interactive decisions, alerts, and changing outcomes. Canva was used for designing the visual assets and our project demonstration, and AI tools were used for code and debugging.

One of the main features we were focused on was giving players meaningful choices. Instead of having an obvious answer, or directly failing the players, the game allows them to continue while showing how each decision costs them over time. A choice that seems helpful at first might create trade-offs or strain resources later, encouraging players to think ahead & weigh long-term consequences and replay to see how different strategies play out.

We also incorporated scientific information inspired by NASA's research and resources to connect the game with real-world space exploration. Features such as the laptop, wristwatch alerts, daily mission logs, and performance based feedback were designed to help make the experience feel more immersive

We also incorporated scientific information inspired by NASA's research and resources to connect the gameplay with real-world space exploration. Features such as the virtual laptop, wristwatch alerts, daily mission logs, and performance-based feedback were designed to make the experience feel more immersive while helping players applying what they learn.

Creativity was the major part of our development process. We went for a cozy, retro pixel art aesthetic to make the game visually appealing and approachable, especially for younger audiences. We focused on keeping the interface simple, challenges easy to understand, and keeping the whole experience enjoyable while balancing scientific accuracy and accessibility for young learners and making the game pace engaging.

Overall, we wanted to show that learning science doesn't always have to feel like studying. Through our game, Mission Lunara, we hope to encourage curiosity, independent thinking, and an interest in the possibilities of space exploration in the future!
